name: Proper Labeled Sample Compression of Full Cube
details: Let $b_n=\min\{k\ge0:\sum_{i=0}^k2^i\binom ni\ge2^n\}$. Writing $n=5q+r$ with $0\le r<5$, we have $b_n\le\mathrm{pLSC}(2^{[n]})\le2q+\lceil r/2\rceil$. Exact for $n=1,2,3,4,5$: $1,1,2,2,2$; also exact at $n=7$, with value three. No exact general formula is asserted.
proof: On five coordinates indexed by $0,\ldots,4$, represent a labeled key by integer masks $(M,Y)$: $M$ records observed coordinates and $Y$ the coordinates labeled one, so $Y$ is a bitwise submask of $M$. A binary reconstructed word $w$ has bit $x$ equal to its label at coordinate $x$. The following complete decoder table lists the outputs for each $M$ in increasing numerical order of its submasks $Y$: $$\begin{array}{r|l} M&\rho(M,Y)\\\hline 0&0\\1&10,9\\2&8,10\\3&24,1,18,11\\4&10,12\\5&10,1,22,21\\6&1,10,4,15\\8&3,10\\9&16,3,10,29\\10&17,3,8,10\\12&3,7,10,14\\16&8,31\\17&8,5,30,27\\18&8,14,25,23\\20&2,13,26,20\\24&6,8,19,28\end{array}$$ For each of the 243 partial samples $(A,B)$ on these coordinates, at least one of the 51 listed keys satisfies $M\subseteq A$, $Y=B\cap M$ and $\rho(M,Y)\cap A=B$, where intersections and inclusions refer to the encoded sets. Choose the first such key in the table order. These finite conditions are exhaustively replayed, with an independent literal-set check, by sync/verify_full_cube_labeled_compression.py. Thus two examples suffice, with no auxiliary message, order or repetition. Every output belongs to the full cube, so the scheme is proper. One example cannot suffice: eleven empty/singleton labeled keys cannot decode all 32 distinct full inputs. Hence the five-cube value is exactly two. For $n=5q+r$, partition the domain in advance into $q$ blocks of size five and a remainder of size $r<5$. Apply this decoder separately to each five-block, and the database-owned stable two-coordinate block scheme to the remainder. The union of all keys has size at most $2q+\lceil r/2\rceil$. The decoder recovers each block's key by restriction to its fixed domain; no decomposition message is needed. Consistency holds on every block and therefore on the full sample. No stability is asserted for the five-block scheme. For the lower bound, the $2^n$ full inputs need different retained keys, of which there are $\sum_{i=0}^k2^i\binom ni$. This gives $b_n$. It matches the stated upper bound for $n=1,2,3,4,5,7$. For all $n$, $\sum_{i=0}^k2^i\binom ni\le4^k\sum_{i=0}^n2^{-i}\binom ni=4^k(3/2)^n$, so $k\ge(n/2)\log_2(4/3)>n/5$. This proves linear order. Ordinary and proper labeled compression coincide on a full cube because every binary total reconstruction belongs to the class.
references: Explicit decoder and counting proof above; solver-free replay in sync/verify_full_cube_labeled_compression.py. The proper stable labeled full-cube proof owns the remainder's two-coordinate scheme.
